thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: deploy-canary connection-drain-failure - high 5xx % on /v1/generate from eu-west canary nodes
Sara L.: I'm seeing a spike in 502/499 from the canary pool, started ~2m after the rollout. Canary was 10%.
Ben K.: Confirmed - dashboards show request latency jumps right before 502s, connection counts for the canary hosts spike and never drop.
Kai W.: Possible TCP CLOSE_WAIT leak during drain. I deployed a small drain-hook change last week; could be related. Marking as P1.
Maria P.: Customer impact? Any big tenants on canary?
Ben K.: A few paid tenants routed to canary for canary-traffic testing. Errors are ~12% of EU traffic to the model endpoint, some requests time out client-side (499).
Sara L.: Runbook step 1: try kill-switch FF to divert traffic off canary. I'll flip the topology flag now: `ffctl --env prod set canary:false`
Sara L.: ops-bot: `ffctl` reports propagation in progress to gateways.
ops-bot: Flag update acknowledged. Propagation to edge proxies: 0/8 -> 5/8 -> 8/8
Darren: Propagation looks done but connection counts are still high on the canary hosts, 1 of 4 nodes shows >1500 ESTABLISHED.
Kai W.: If connections are stuck they won't drain, so traffic still reaches those sockets until closed. Looking at process list on node-3 now.
Ben K.: Rolling traffic off via dynamic routing as well: `routectl set-weight canary 0` to be safe. Doing that now.
Sara L.: routectl reports success. New inbound traffic at the canary LB dropped to ~2% but errors persist for requests hitting node-3 directly (health check indicates unhealthy responses 502).
Maria P.: I'll check the customer dashboard and open a support note for affected tenants. Tagging support: @support-team - we're escalating.
Darren: node-3 logs show repeated `send() EPIPE` and `accept()` backlog warnings. Kernel tcp_fin_timeout is high; connections piling up.
Kai W.: Running `lsof -p <modelproc>` shows many sockets in `CLOSE_WAIT`. Process not calling `close()`. Could be a libc change from recent build.
Sara L.: We need to stop new work on the process to let it unwind. Starting a graceful restart of the model worker on node-3: `systemctl restart model-worker@3 --graceful --timeout=30s`
Ben K.: Restart failed to gracefully drain - process still holds FDs after restart attempt. Moving to hard restart. Notifying oncall escalation.
incident-bot: @pager escalated to primary-oncall: Ben K.
Ben K.: Hard restart now. `systemctl kill -s SIGKILL model-worker@3` then `systemctl start model-worker@3`.
ops-bot: node-3 model-worker restarted, connection counts dropped to normal within 40s. Health checks green.
Maria P.: Customer impact update: initial estimate ~15 minutes of elevated errors for a small subset of EU customers. Filing an incident summary for status page.
Sara L.: Root cause hypothesis: regress in drain-hook/new runtime change causing file descriptor leak under high concurrency, surfaced only on canary because of different client IP mix.
Kai W.: I'll open a PR to revert last week's drain-hook patch and run a quick repro on staging. Tagging `eng-runtime` for follow-up.
Darren: For immediate safety, we should also add a guard in the deploy pipeline: if connection drain > x seconds or ESTABLISHED > y, abort staged rollout.
Sara L.: Agreed. I'll file a TODO and add it to the rollout checklist.
Ben K.: Rolling the canary forward carefully: re-enable canary at 0% then 5% with new monitoring thresholds. Waiting 10m before increasing.
Maria P.: Support note updated and customer-facing message drafted: "We investigated a partial service disruption for EU model endpoints during a canary deploy. Traffic diverted and nodes restarted; service restored. We will follow up with a root-cause and mitigation plan."
Sara L.: Handoff to night shift: @Kai W. you're on primary for next 6h. Ben will remain available for rapid consult.
Kai W.: Got it. I'll monitor the canary for the next 6 hours and validate the revert PR once merged.
incident-bot: Incident closed to oncall channel: severity downgraded to P2, follow-up actions assigned to eng-runtime.
Ben K.: Postmortem items: 1) revert faulty drain-hook, 2) add deploy-time guard for connection drain/established thresholds, 3) add automated kill-switch test in CI to validate flag propagation, 4) customer RCA by EOD.
Sara L.: Thanks everyone. I'll start the postmortem doc and assign owners. :thumbsup:
